analysis: Unary rewriting games coincide with octal games (Dawson's Kayles, Officers, 0.007, 0.06, 0.4); Dawson's Kayles and 0.4 have period 34 (Guy-Smith window verified); Officers, 0.007, 0.06 show no period <= 300 up to n = 3000; a^14 has Grundy value 4 under aa -> b.
assumptions: Guy-Smith periodicity theorem for finite octal games
counterexamples: aa -> b: Grundy value of a^14 is 4 (H-C04-6 refuted)
falsification: Any n <= 20 where the word game, the run game and the octal recursion disagree; a Grundy value >= 4 refutes H-C04-6.

hypothesis: H-C04-7: on the word a^n, the game of aa -> b (also bb, bbb, bab) is Dawson's Kayles 0.07; aa -> ab (also ba, abb, bba) is Officers 0.6; aaa -> b (bb, bbb, bab) is 0.007; aaa -> ab (ba, abb, bba) is 0.06; aaa -> aba is 0.4. H-C04-6 (bold, from EXP-C04-07): Grundy values of rewriting games in the family never exceed 3.
methodology: (1) Grundy value of the single word a^n from its exact derivation graph (no decomposition), n <= 20, compared with the octal recursion and with the generic run-game recursion. (2) Octal Grundy values to n = 3000; smallest period p <= 300 with preperiod n0 holding over the whole range, and the Guy-Smith window n0 <= n < 2 n0 + p + t checked explicitly.
question: Which classical take-and-break games are the rewriting games of rules a^k -> u?
